title: The column rank is at most the row rank, with no hypothesis
statement: For every matrix M over the constructed rationals and all dimensions rows and cols, Rat.rankCols M rows cols is at most Rat.rank M rows cols. UNCONDITIONALLY: no section hypothesis and no echelon-form obligation. F:rat-rank-eq-rank-cols-of-pivot-section gives the two counts as EQUAL but has to assume the section hypothesis, because the cross-bound counting law it goes through needs a constructive inverse; the inequality in this direction needs only the injection, and the two hypotheses that costs are exactly the two the bridge already discharges from its two searches.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.rankCols_le_rank : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Rat))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat.le (Rat.rankCols x0 x1 x2) (Rat.rank x0 x1 x2))))

evidence.supports: Rat.rankCols_le_rank is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(target/release/examples/kernel_declaration_projection 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cF -e '-> AxNat.le (Rat.rankCols x0 x1 x2) (Rat.rank x0 x1 x2))))')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is a DISTINGUISHING substring of the admitted type, not the declaration's name: an existence check would still pass if the statement drifted. Verified to hit ZERO on a perturbed pattern before this row was written -- see the mutation table in ADR-1593. `kernel_declaration_projection` prints every declaration with its footprint size and its rendered type, and the prelude build admits this theorem only through the trusted gate, so a successful build IS the type-check. `grep -cF -e` rather than `grep -cF`: a pattern beginning with `-` is parsed as an OPTION, and five of these seven do. The table in ADR-1593 caught that -- the rows failed as written before `-e` was added, which is why it was run at all.

evidence.notes: A `rankCols_le_rank` that had quietly kept the section hypothesis would still be called that and would still be admitted. `rat_prelude/rank_bridge_tests.rs` reads the declared type out of the environment and forbids `Rat.nonzeroRowB` (the section hypothesis cannot be stated without it) and the transposed bound (a different theorem, and one that is NOT free -- in that orientation the injectivity obligation is ADR-1554 obligation 4).

notes: The consumer of F:nat-countrange-le-of-injon, and the point of that lemma in one line. rank_bridge.rs's own table records which of Nat.countRange_bij's five hypotheses cost what: H1 (injectivity of the pivot-row map) and H2 (it sends a pivot column to a nonzero row) are discharged from the two SEARCHES alone and know nothing about echelon form, while H5 -- the inverse's round trip -- is the residue taken as the section hypothesis. Nat.countRange_le_of_injOn takes exactly H1 and H2, so tau never appears and neither does the section. The asymmetry is real and this statement does not paper over it: the REVERSE direction, rank <= rankCols, is what bounds rank by cols and still needs the section, because in that orientation the injectivity obligation is injectivity of the leading index on the nonzero rows, which IS ADR-1554 obligation 4. ADR-1593.
